column1: # The words venues bill AROUND a film, by concept and language — one table, read by every rule that recognises them
# (services.movies.TitleWords; which reader reads which concept is in TitleWords.Concept's doc). A word missing here is
# missing everywhere at once, so TitleWordsSpec fails when a concept lacks a word in any language a country bills in
# (pl, de, en, es) — a German "Jubiläum" the English and Spanish lists never knew is a test failure, not a prod regression.
#   phrase: written as venues write it (case and accents kept: readers fold them). Words are separated by spaces; a
#   trailing `*` makes a word a stem ("podwójn*" = podwójny, podwójne…), a leading one lets a phrase start inside a
#   word. Concepts read as WORD SETS take every word of a phrase ("Q&A" = q, a) and allow no `*`.
# ── anniversary: a re-release celebrating the film's anniversary ("30th Anniversary", "35-jähriges Jubiläum") ──

column4: Der mit dem Wolf tanzt (35-jähriges Jubiläum) — DE, 2026-10

column1: # ── edition: a cut, a restoration, a re-release of the same film ──

column4: Metropolis (rest. Fassung 2010) dates a restoration, not the film — 6d6e10830

column1: # ── premiere: a premiere or preview screening ──
# ── talk: a talk, Q&A or introduction around the screening ──
# ── screening: the screening billed as an event of its own ──
# ── film-festival: a FILM festival's own name — billed alone, it is the festival's programme ("Alpen Film Festival 2026") ──
#   a leading `*` reads it inside a compound ("ALPENFILMFESTIVAL", "FreerideFilmFestival")
# ── festival-edition: a film festival's touring edition, billed after its name ("Freeride Filmfestival 2026 CINEMA EDITION") ──
# ── relay: a live relay or broadcast ──
# ── performance: a concert billed with (or as) the screening ──
# ── marathon: a night of several films ──
# ── side-event: what a bill joins after a film when it names an event, not a work ("OPĘTANIE + TRASA PLAKATOWA") ──
# ── old-film: a retrospective, a classic, an archive print, a silent film ──
# ── sneak: a blind screening sold under the sneak's own name — no film to list (the scrape filter drops it) ──
# ── secret-screening: a withheld film billed as an event — listed, never a film the databases hold ──

column4: inert in NonFilmEvents (its "seans" bills a film attached); the scrape filter's sneak drops it first

column1: # ── double-bill: two or more films on one ticket ──

column4: not "zestaw" (a set): a set of a series' episodes is one compilation record

column1: # ── audience: a screening for a special audience — a note no film's title ends on ──
# ── stage-house: an opera or ballet house whose relay a title bills ("Paris Opera Ballett: …", "Tosca (ROH)") ──
# ── stage: a theatre or a staged show ──
# ── stage-show: a word naming the staged show itself, never a strand's name — a staging even heading the billing ──
# ── house-banner: a house's or a relay series' banner and its season ("Met Opera 2026/27: …", "NT Live") ──
# ── short-film: a short billed as one — a venue screening a short says so (ShortFilms.billsAShort) ──
# ── director-credit: the word a venue bills its film's director after, inside the title ("Lalka, reż. Maciej Kawalski
# (2026)", "Alpha (dir. Ducournau)") — read into the listing's director at intake (TitleFacts), each country in its own
# languages and English. A name must follow, capitalised: "mit Regie-Besuch!" credits nobody ──
# ── original-title: the label a venue bills a film's original title after, inside the title ("(Originaltitel: La petite
# cuisine de Mehdi)") — read into the listing's original title at intake (TitleFacts) ──
